question: What must tad in Rust be, and how should it declare its tables?
found: tad today: a 127-line runner (check, canonical form, SQL statements on DuckDB) and a 478-line renderer of Markdown documents, vendored into four repositories (the phone project, the canon, the playbook, Rhizoid). Their schemas hold 41 tables, and every constraint is an id pattern, a list of allowed values, a required field, or one list-of-words column - no foreign keys, no SQL logic. So tables can be declared as data (Frictionless Table Schema, CSV on the Web), checked without a database engine; SQL stays a possible view onto the data (as Datasette is), not its source of truth. Dolt keeps a database in a separate store; tad keeps text in plain git, which is its point. Measured 2026-11-11: Python's check only compares field names with columns; the real validation is canon (DuckDB enforces types and rules on import), and checks/*.sql holds 13 cross-table invariants of four kinds - ids unique across tables, references resolving, everything cited, no mirrored relations - all declarable as data. Measured 2026-11-11: three of the four repositories carry an older vendored copy of the renderer (185 and 194 lines against today's 478) - copies drift silently. On the switch the canon and Rhizoid get today's renderer for the first time; their documents change (rule lines between log entries, reStructuredText if asked).
